key_insight: Delete-one-configuration jackknife covariance with conformal scaling gives linear ACE potentials more reliable uncertainty estimates than a calibrated Bayesian posterior.
engineering_relevance: Calibrated force and property intervals can help engineers judge the reliability of silicon simulations involving elasticity, surfaces, cracks, and defects.
method: Estimate parameter covariance by leaving out one training configuration at a time.
Apply a held-out conformal scale to calibrate per-atom force uncertainty.
Propagate parameter uncertainty to relaxed silicon properties using implicit differentiation and committees.
evidence_signal: Tests covered held-out silicon forces, excluded cracks and screw dislocations, and 21 DFT-referenced properties; the larger model produced property intervals about four times tighter, while POPS force coverage was 0.95 and 0.84 at a nominal 0.90.
watch_item: Jackknife uncertainty misses bias shared across training configurations: relaxed point-defect coverage needed a discrepancy correction devised after inspecting property results.
paper_title: Jackknife-conformal uncertainty for linear ACE potentials: calibrated forces and silicon properties compared with Bayesian and POPS baselines
